page: Microsoft Azure D2as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv5 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture, running at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The instance features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, but it is Premium Storage capable. There are no integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng is strong, ranking in the top 25% with a score of 2700.18. However, multi-core performance is weak, also scoring 2700.18, which falls into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is generally constrained, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 128.68 GB/sec and uncached large block read and write speeds at 32.41 GB/sec and 22.32 GB/sec respectively. Single-threaded compression tasks perform at average levels, with gzip compression reaching 25.96 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 11.36 GB/sec.

Given its hardware profile, the D2as_v5 represents an entry-tier general-purpose option. It exhibits poor performance in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput. LLM inference speeds for a small 135M model are also limited, with prompt processing at 128.99 tokens per second. The instance is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic development environments, or low-traffic web serving where high multi-core throughput and massive memory bandwidth are not required.
